p.seg: Note that until the 19th century the title of this book was 商子 in the bibliographies (but note that•Inthe old commentary to 三國志，蜀書，先主傳 we have “閒暇歷觀諸子及《六韜》商君書 “(perhaps not yet a book title but a description of a set of documents) the book of the Lord of Shang” 益人意智。”just as the title of HFZ was 韓子 until Song times.•It is striking that both HFZ and SJS have opening chapters that are transmitted elsewhere as attributed to other authors, and in the same Han dynasty compilation, the 戰國策.•新序書證 lays out the parallel versions very conveniently. ••《更法》like 《定分》is explitly and expressly an account by someone other than Shang Yang who is mentioned in these two chapers as a third person 公孫鞅. Note that the 孟子 is explicitly not written by the 孟子 therein mentioned in the third person.•(We still do not have a good survey of the history of explicit andimplicit authorial self-reference in ancient Chinese literature.)

•This refers to a formal session and not just to an occasion where Duke Xiao was evaluating his plans, I think. 張覺 2012 quotes 淮南子 平詞訟，注： “平，治也” and translates: “研究治國的策略“•LordXiao was working on his strategy for the future.•于暢and王紹爛find the phrase unreadable and write 平晝閒居•Forour detailed interpretation of the nature of discursive governance andconsultative decision-making inancient China, the passage is instructive. •Wenote that there is no record of any acceptance by the participants in the consultation ofthe decision made and implemented by the ruler, •andthat 孝公 does not participate in the discussion except to approve and decide.

•Thisidentifies the consensual legitimisation group which 孝公 needs to justify his political/administrative decisions.•Nonobility implied here, no aristocracy: •“Threenobles” is misleading.•大夫 are generically incumbents of high rank positions: “dignitaries". •Perelomov 1968: три сановника в ранге дафу. is a satisfactory paraphrase.
•Vogelsang’s ”sich wandelten” and Pines ”the changes” for 變 fails to recognise the nuance of radical currentchange in 變。

•正法 is a verb-object construction.•“discussedthe basis of correct laws” seriously misconstrues the syntax.•張覺 spells out explicitly that 正 is causative here, and he isfollowed by 石磊 who points to the phrase 正法則 in Xunzi.•Perelomov: о сушности исправления законов.•北京電子管廠1976:創立新法 is careless.
What is sought after isthe (RIGHT PROPER) method 北京電子管廠1976 helpfully unpacks theopaque concept of 道 in a way that is all too rare: 道：原則，方法 使民 is not a matter of “employ”。

•代立 •”whentaking over from one's predecessor“•NOT: 即位 "bei der Thronbesteigung" as ogelsang has it.•Duyvendak had it right: “at his succession”. Pines forgets about this phrase.•忘 is here, as often, •忽略 "be delinquent in the care of: benegligent with, fail to be properly preoccupied by" the altars of state>the nation/. We have abstract Synekdochē here.•не забывать is perhaps acceptable because of its continuative nuance.•社稷 is figurative and does not in fact refer to the phyical objects of these symbols of state.The reference is to “(the interests of) the nation”.•
•北京電子管廠1976 yet again splendidly unpacks the specific content of 道 in a useful way: 道：本分也。

•主長 "superior" is a hendiadys according to Gao Heng.•主長 is then abstract “leader/head/superior” NOT sovereign as Pines has it.•This 主長 is NOT a sovereign, the Zhou kingis.•He isprobably subject to the King as the sovereign person who has enfeoffed him. •(Thathe may be the de facto sovereign is another matter.)•張覺 reads zhǔ cháng “the superior’s strong points”.•as does the Russian: чтобы всем были ясны достоинства правителя.•北京電子管廠1976: 長：長處

•變法 is specifically “(fundamentally) change the legal arrangements", is not at all the same as Pines’s “change the laws”. Liang Wanru 2017 has it beautifully: 改革法制. I find this rendering perfect.•modifyor change the laws to the better is 更法, completely transform the legal system". •易法 would be "replace (the old) laws (with new ones)" •變 is abrupt major change, politically often “revolution".•изменить законы is no better than the English.•Vogelsang’s “nun will ich die Regeln aendern um zu regieren” does not get the nuance of 變法 and fails to understand 以治 ”in order achieve (good) governance” "orderly rule" as Pines has it very nicely.

••Am terrified that there will be public criticism of me.•Public critical debate/discussion is an interesting social institutionin classical China.•There is a different vocabulary (非 etc) for personal criticism.•опасаюсь что поднебесная осудит меня. is also too weak on the fear, andmisconstrues 議 public criticism as condemnation.天下 “Everyone under the sun” does not, of course, refer to everyoneunder the sun: it refers in fact to members of the rulin class primarily within thestate. Vogelsang’s German “alle Welt” is suitably short andsingularly apt. •Поднебесная
臣 “you subject" is generally submissive and and assertive of one's high status in the hierarchy, as Pines has it. Vogelsang's "Euer Untertan" has it right.
疑行 "be half-hearted in public action"
疑事 "be half-hearted in the implementation of public business"; 無 “never"

亟定 “must urgently fix, determine" is not "concentrate your thoughts on" as Pines has it, who disregards 亟. Vogelsang‘s "habt bereits den festen Entschluss gefasst" forgets that the Duke seeks advice on what to do, and disregards 亟 "quickly>urgently".

•Pines “he who whose thinking is exceptionally perceptive” •is disappointing here on a crucial intellectual point of this dialogue.•獨知 is the buzzword here, and it isnot about perceptiveness but about “intellectual independence (of judgment)”.•Gongsun Yang is zeroing in on the essenceof his opposition to traditionalism. •I think the idea is “anyone who engages in intellectuallyindependent thinking/planning”, who has emancipated itself from adherence to traditionalist cultural correctness.•Vogelsang’s ” und wer eigenständige Gedanken hegt,” is much to be preferred to the English versions.•“A planner who has independent 獨特的 understanding”???
The Shiji quotes this line from 商君書 as 必見訾於人。 The meaning of "言 under 敖" remains obscure to me: maybe it is indeed "ridicule".

Pines: “are blind even to the things that are accomplished” will not do. Zhang Jue has it perfectly: 既成的事实.•"The stupid are in the dark (even) about things that are (already) manifest/have already taken open form”•Vogelsang has a perfect reading of this line: “‚Die Dummen sind selbst für vollendete Tatsachen blind,”•成 does not here mean “accomplish”but as often elsewhere “take complete form”.

"the clever sees things before they have even budded" is quite extraordinary, and quite different from Pines's conventional "grasp [the matter] in the bud". Vogelsang has it beautifully: "erblickt sie schon, bevor sie aufkeimen".

Perelomov: но можно вместе с ним наслаждаться завершением [дел]: 成 is nab perfective “completion, manifest realisation". 樂成 "enjoy the completion/manifest realisation" goes together. Pines's "rejoice with them" disregards the grammar. Gemini is interesting because it gets close to the essence: "but they can share in the joy of its completion".
•論至德： 至 is superlative. Pines’s ”superb virtue” gets this subtly wrong.•Duyvendak already got the point: ”the highest virtue”. •Gemini does have it very precisely: ”ultimate virtue”.
•the 對仗 between 俗 and 眾 does not NECESSARILY mean that 俗 here has to refer to vulgar people. 待考
•所以愛民也 ”is a means by which to take good care for the people”, is misconstrued in Pines ”is to care for the people”. Same misconstruction in the next line. Gao Heng is similarly careless: 是爱护人民的。

•所以愛民也 ”is a means by which to take good care for the people”, is misconstrued in Pines ”is to care for the people”. Same misconstruction in the next line.•Liang Wanru has it right I think: ” 是为了便于处理事情。”•Zhang Jue is easy to misunderstand: “是用来方便办事的。” He surely does not mean what he appears to say.•Gemini gets everything straight: “that by which affairs are made convenient.”

•“whenever one will really>definitely (故訓匯纂 passim:苟,誠也) thereby to strengthen the state, the sage willdeviate from ancient prededent; •Pines’s “Hence whenever it is possible to strengthen hisstate, the sage does not emulate the past; “ does not get the philosophical point of this.

•We have here a politically important case of what M.M. Bakhtin called жанры речи “genres of speech” with its Sprachregelungen.•Only the convenor of the “legitimising consensus group” himself canuse this authoritative expression of immediate but temporary approbation. Moreover, the convener does not himself undertake to make his ownindependent proposals.•Similarly, only the convenor of the legitimising consensus group himself can 從之 “follow the advice”, and only the convenor can 不聽 “refuse to follow the advice.•No one merely convened can do more than agree by “然。” and the like.
"I diagree!"
Whether Gan Long was or was not a minister is quite irrelevant in this context: "your subject". As above.
"will not (try to) change the people (into anything new) on order to instruct them,
"the competent person will not (try to) change the legal system in order to govern them well:
since he adapts to the people (as they are) in order to teach them (well)
without any hard labour his work will be done;
since he relies on the legal system (as it is) in order to govern well,
officials will perform their routines and the people will be comfortable.
Not: "your words", but "what you are putting forward"!
"ordinary people are at peace with what is traditional and well rehearsed": "what he has become accustomed to in the past" misconstrues the grammar.
"scholars drown in what they have been taught." 溺 cannot mean "stick to" in this sense, I think.
守法 “adhere to the law" is standard. Preserving the law (as it is) is in any case not at issue in this line.

"but these are not the kind with whom on discusses matters beyond the law (currently in effect)." The reference is to such matters as the possible fundamental change of the legal system, as Zhang Jue (mistakenly) writes into his translation: 而不能和他们塔轮变革法制的事.
"The three Dynasties, with their different ritual protocols did achieve royal authority"
A person constrained by (THE PREVAILING) regime of rituals
is unqualified to debate undertakings WItH
is restricted by (THE PREVAILING) laws
is unqualified to discuss fundamental change with.
You, my lord, should never be in any doubt about this
I, your subject, am told that
"unless the resulting benefit is increased thereby a hundred times
unless the results obtained are thereby improved tenfold
"by modelling oneself on the ancients one never goes wrong
by following (prevailing) ritual protocol one never commits evil:
You, my lord, must take this into account."
What antiquity is one to model oneself on?
and when it came to Kings Wen and Wu
they each established laws in response to their moments in time
and they established ritual procedures based on the needs for their undertakings.
Ritual and legal systems have (always) been fixed in accordance with the (changing) times
legal provisions were, in each case, matters of expedience.
arms and tools were, in each case, adapted to their specific use.
Your subject concludes:
For governing one's own era is not (always) by one one and the same method.
for being of use to one's state one does not necessarily have to model oneself on the ancients.
When Tang and Wu became kings,
it was not that they rose by following the ancients;
When the Yin and the Xia were destroyed
it was that because they replaced existing ritual protocols that they were undone.
Hence it follows that when somebody goes against the ancients that does not prove he is necessarily doing wrong;
and when someone follows existing ritual protocol that is not sufficient to show that he is predominantly right.
You should be in no doubt, my lord.
I'm told that in the slums people are prone to find things strange.
Parochial scholars are often nit-picking.
the joys of a madman
area worthy's worry.
constrained by the conventions of their time, may people criticise me
I shall have no longer any doubt on this matter.
At that point he issued the (famous) Order to Cultivate Wastelands.
